outputs.final_proof:
\begin{proof}
By De Moivre's formula,
\[
\left(\cos(1^\circ)+i\sin(1^\circ)\right)^{360}=\cos(360^\circ)+i\sin(360^\circ)=1.
\]
Thus $z=\cos(1^\circ)+i\sin(1^\circ)$ satisfies $z^{360}-1=0$, with $z^{360}-1\in\mathbb{Q}[X]$, and is therefore algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$. Its conjugate $\overline z$ is also algebraic. Since
\[
\cos(1^\circ)=\frac{z+\overline z}{2},
\]
and algebraic numbers are closed under addition and division by nonzero rational numbers, $\cos(1^\circ)$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$.\end{proof}
